papers.title: REM Sleep Iota Oscillations Across the Lifespan
papers.summary: Analyzed high-density sleep EEG from 937 individuals aged 7-70 to characterize REM sleep iota oscillations (25-40 Hz), finding prevalence declining from 88% in children to 44% in older adults and age-related shifts in peak frequency, amplitude, topography, and bandwidth. Twin analyses revealed high heritability of most iota properties except bandwidth, establishing iota as a genetically determined trait-like REM sleep marker.

papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, flickering light stimulation during deprivation prevented upregulation of activity-dependent and unfolded protein response (ER stress) genes while further increasing NREM slow-wave activity, and induced brief neuronal OFF periods resembling sleep-like cortical states. The authors conclude that physiological manipulation of cortical activity can dissociate molecular ER-stress signatures from electrophysiological sleep-pressure markers.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 31 adults undergoing propofol-based gastrointestinal endoscopy, portable polysomnography-derived six-channel EEG captured stage-related changes across baseline, induction, maintenance, and recovery, including decreasing relative delta power, increasing theta/alpha/sigma/beta power and SEF95, and highest spindle-like event density during recovery. Amplitude envelope correlation showed the most widespread stage-related connectivity differences, identifying candidate EEG markers for emergence detection and atypical anesthetic-state identification.

papers.title: Comparing re-referencing methods for human intracranial EEG
papers.summary: This study compared re-referencing methods on macro-contact and microwire SEEG data from 16 epilepsy patients performing an episodic memory task, finding that method choice altered artifact-rejection survival, low-frequency power, and aperiodic background. In hippocampal recordings, however, no method changed the magnitude or direction of the memory effect in power or spike-field coherence.

papers.title: Dynamics-informed machine learning for recovering extensive missing systems dynamics.
papers.summary: The authors introduce Full-Partial Reconstruction Mapping (FPRM), a dynamics-informed imputation framework that embeds state-space reconstruction priors and learns diffeomorphic topology between attractors from complete and incomplete data. Across model systems (including coupled 120D Lorenz and Rössler systems) and real datasets, FPRM reliably imputed multiple variables even when only one variable was fully observed and others had up to 90% missingness, outperforming traditional approaches.

papers.title: Beyond Mean Pooling: Statistical Meta-Aggregation for Subject-Level EEG Classification in Parkinson's Disease
papers.summary: The authors propose statistical meta-aggregation that summarizes each subject's epoch-wise EEG predictions with 14 distribution descriptors instead of mean pooling, using a self-supervised contrastive encoder in 90 subjects (57 Parkinson's disease, 33 controls). Replacing mean pooling raised subject-level ROC-AUC from 0.655 to 0.872 for logistic regression and from 0.724 to 0.840 for SVM without changing the encoder or classifier family.

papers.title: How Much of Cross-Subject EEG Emotion Recognition Is Stimulus Memorization?
papers.summary: The authors adapted three representation-level shortcut diagnostics to published contrastive cross-subject EEG emotion encoders and found stimulus identity was linearly recoverable at six to fifteen times chance. When subjects and stimuli were held out jointly, each released classifier lost two to forty-four accuracy points, indicating that headline accuracies from subject hold-out alone reflect stimulus memorization rather than cross-subject emotion decoding.

papers.title: EEG-Based Characterization of Cortical Dynamics during Graded Resistance Exercise.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Recorded EEG in ten healthy participants performing bicep curls across five resistance levels and found resistance-dependent differences in movement-related cortical potentials and spectral power, with a triplet temporal convolutional network plus KNN classifier reaching 97.2% within-subject and 93.0% subject-independent accuracy in discriminating resistance conditions.

papers.title: MULTIMODAL EEG WORLD MODEL: SELF-SUPERVISED LATENT TRANSITION LEARNING FOR WEARABLE EEG SEIZURE DETECTION
papers.summary: The authors propose a self-supervised Multimodal EEG World Model that predicts the latent representation of the next EEG segment conditioned on synchronized ECG, EMG, and movement signals via query-based fusion, with label-free pretraining and a frozen encoder plus linear probe downstream. On SeizeIT2 with a strict patient-wise split it achieved AUPRC 0.3748, ROC-AUC 0.8025, and balanced accuracy 0.7308, outperforming database and external baselines and showing a 14.4% relative AUPRC gain over a random-initialized encoder.

papers.title: Daytime Napping and Associative-Memory Retrieval Speed: An Exploratory Behavioral and EEG Study
papers.summary: In a within-participant exploratory study of 15 healthy students, daytime napping was associated with 6.7% faster delayed associative recognition (significant Condition-by-Time interaction, b = -0.063, p = .027) while monitored wakefulness produced no change, with the difference concentrated among slower responses; accuracy did not differ by condition. Nap EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger periodic sigma activity, but no EEG measure explained the response-time effect.

papers.title: Delineating neural contributions to electroencephalogram-based speech decoding.
papers.summary: Applied explainable AI to a convolutional neural network decoding spoken words from ultra-high-density EEG and showed that electrode contributions could not be explained by EMG mutual information, with contributing time periods overlapping between overt and covert speech. Denoising enhanced contributions from speech-related brain areas, supporting EEG-based neural speech decoding after appropriate preprocessing.

papers.title: CNN-based classifier for subject-independent MBTI Extraversion/Introversion preference classification from short-time EEG signals
papers.summary: Compared EEGNet, EEGProgress, and a new compact CNN (SSCNet) for subject-independent classification of MBTI extraversion/introversion from 4-s EEG segments in 50 participants; SSCNet achieved the highest mean accuracy (0.6481), AUC (0.7063), and F1 (0.6276) with lowest fold variability and best computational efficiency.

papers.title: A feature-optimized EEG framework using multiscale entropy and metaheuristic optimization for cognitive analysis.
papers.summary: The study applied multiscale entropy features (dispersion, permutation, sample, fuzzy) with filter- and wrapper-based feature selection to EEG from 100 participants to distinguish sports from non-sports groups. Genetic Algorithm optimization yielded a minimal feature subset with 93.0 ± 2.7% nested cross-validated accuracy using SVM, and five classifiers showed mean Fleiss' kappa of 0.874 ± 0.051.

papers.title: The spatial extent of fast ripples is associated with cognitive and language deficits in children with focal epilepsy: An exploratory SEEG study.
papers.summary: In 30 pediatric focal epilepsy patients undergoing SEEG, the spatial extent of interictal fast ripples (250-500 Hz) during NREM sleep was associated with cognitive deficit severity (p=0.049), while fast ripple rates in inferior frontal gyrus, superior temporal gyrus, and basal temporal language regions correlated with language deficits (r up to 0.79); ripples and IEDs showed weaker associations.

papers.title: ADHDeepNet: An Explainable Framework for EEG-Based ADHD Detection From Raw Signals.
papers.summary: Introduced ADHDeepNet, a deep learning framework combining temporal-spatial characterization, attention modules, and explainability for EEG-based ADHD detection, achieving 99.17% accuracy and 100% sensitivity in classifying 61 ADHD and 60 healthy control participants under nested cross-validation.

papers.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study synchronized mobile EEG and eye tracking via LabStreamingLayer during a simplified director task to compute overlap-corrected regression-based ERPs time-locked to spoken nouns and fixations. Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity, fixation timing modulated neural responses, and competitors received little visual attention; analysis scripts and datasets are openly available.

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state EEG microstates in 68 patients with psychotic depression versus 63 with non-psychotic depression, finding prolonged microstate C duration and altered transition probabilities (increased B→A, decreased B→C and C→A) in the psychotic group, with reduced B→C transition most robustly associated with thought disturbance and hostility.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: Built an intelligent assessment framework combining task-state ERP-derived alpha-band power spectral densities and coherence with motor function scores from 78 prolonged disorders of consciousness patients; linear SVM and logistic regression under leave-one-out cross-validation achieved macro-average F1 around 76% and AUC around 72-78%.

papers.title: [Spectral-topographic features of EEG in patients with varying rates of alcohol dependence progression].
papers.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
papers.summary: Compared background EEG spectral-topographic features in 40 male alcohol-dependent patients with rapid (≤3 years, n=23) versus slow (≥12 years, n=17) disease progression, finding significantly reduced alpha-1 power across all regions (strongest frontocentrally) plus reduced alpha-2, theta, and frontal beta-1 power in rapid progressors, with 74% showing low-amplitude flattened EEG.

papers.title: Region-Specific EEG Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using a Sliding-Window 2D CNN: A Subject-Independent Evaluation
papers.summary: Used a sliding-window 2D CNN on 256-channel EEG from 62 participants to classify hypnotic susceptibility by brain region; random-split results (e.g., occipital accuracy 0.721) collapsed under leave-one-subject-out validation (occipital 0.453), whereas frontal and prefrontal regions retained above-chance LOSO accuracy (0.646 and 0.624).

papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Electroencephalography in Hypnosis: A Neurophysiological Approach.
papers.journal: The International journal of clinical and experimental hypnosis
papers.summary: This review synthesizes EEG evidence on the neural correlates of hypnosis, reporting that theta power is stronger in highly hypnotizable individuals and relates to hypnotic depth, while gamma activity links to focus and suggestion acceptance. It further describes frequency-dependent reorganization of frontal-parietal and attentional network connectivity, left-hemisphere activation patterns, and ERP effects on pre-attentional and cognitive processing.

papers.title: EEG-Based Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using Two-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.summary: Applied 2D CNNs to minimally preprocessed 256-channel EEG from 62 male participants to classify hypnotic susceptibility during Guided Imagery, evaluating models across brain regions and time windows with LOSO cross-validation. Best single-window random-split accuracy was 0.82, while under LOSO the frontal region reached mean accuracy 0.646 (AUC 0.692), improving to 0.738 with a 10-window ensemble; the occipital region fell to near-chance, implicating anterior regions as most generalizable markers.

papers.title: Advanced Detection of Pre-Ictal Stages in Epilepsy Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Automated Feature Extraction.
papers.summary: The study developed a convolutional neural network model with automated feature extraction and LSTM/SVM-based classification to detect the pre-ictal phase of epileptic seizures using the CHB-MIT scalp EEG dataset. It reports pre-ictal state detection evaluated by sensitivity and specificity with an initial two-second window configuration.

papers.title: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality.
papers.summary: In a VR-based upper-limb motor training study with 14 neurotypical participants, augmented sensory feedback modality and task difficulty differentially modulated behavioral, physiological, and perceptual outcomes, with visual+haptic feedback during straight-line training yielding the largest reductions in path length and completion time.

papers.title: Mobile EEG Reveals Age-Dependent Cognitive-Motor Interference with Increasing Motor Task Complexity- a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Compared younger and older adults on behavioral and mobile EEG measures during an oddball choice-reaction task performed while sitting, standing, and treadmill walking to assess cognitive-motor interference. Older adults walked with shorter steps and were generally slower, with response-time slowing extending to walking only in older adults; P3 amplitude decreased during walking in both groups, and P3 latencies were delayed in older adults and associated with longer response times.

papers.title: Generalized Spike-Wave discharges and myoclonic features in a subgroup of children with Self-Limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes.
papers.summary: Retrospectively reviewed 148 children with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) and identified 9 (6.1%) with generalized spike-wave discharges (GSWD), comparing them with patients without GSWD. The GSWD subgroup more often had wakefulness seizures, sleep-related generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and myoclonic manifestations, and two long-followed patients evolved toward juvenile myoclonic epilepsy electroclinically.

papers.title: EEG-defined differences in functional networks following beta-band transcranial alternating current stimulation in patients with disorders of consciousness: a pilot study.
papers.summary: Applied 30-minute frontal 20 Hz tACS (1 mA) to 28 patients with disorders of consciousness and used fNIRS to measure hemoglobin-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical network properties before and after stimulation. tACS was associated with transient enhancement of frontal functional connectivity and acute network reorganization (increased clustering coefficient, global efficiency, and local efficiency; decreased path length) that resolved by the second post-stimulation measurement, with effects dependent on baseline vEEG pathology and Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores correlating with connectivity and efficiency measures.

papers.title: [Neurocognitive characteristics in children with sluggish cognitive tempo].
papers.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
papers.summary: This study compared 40 children with sluggish cognitive tempo (SCT) to 30 with combined ADHD and 30 healthy controls using SCT scales, fatigue and sleepiness measures, working memory and reading tests, the TOVA, and EEG, finding greater asthenic symptoms and reduced anterior theta-to-alpha power ratio in SCT. After Cortexin treatment, 82% of SCT patients showed improvements in inattention, working memory, asthenia, and reading, with reduced frontal-central alpha power suggesting enhanced cortical activation.

papers.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided systematic review of seven studies (three RCTs, four non-randomised; n=390) synthesised clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD. RCTs showed small, generally non-significant effects versus controls, while naturalistic and personalised protocols reported large symptom reductions; no treatment-related adverse events were observed.

papers.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
papers.summary: Evaluated a TMS-evoked potential (TEP)-based assessment (Delphi-MD) for predicting sustained response to ventriculoperitoneal shunt in 41 patients with possible idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus, with 18 shunted patients followed over one year. Higher baseline M1L waveform adherence (WFA) distinguished responders from non-responders with ROC-AUC 0.935 and, at a LOOCV-derived cutoff, achieved 90.9% sensitivity, 85.7% specificity, and 88.9% accuracy, whereas the cerebrospinal fluid tap test did not predict shunt responsiveness.

papers.title: Functional and Organic Pseudo-Orthostatic Tremor: Clinical Features, Electrophysiology, and Treatment Outcomes in a Retrospective Cohort
papers.summary: In a retrospective two-centre cohort of 35 patients with pseudo-orthostatic tremor, 6 (17%) showed features of functional neurological disorder, and among 29 organic cases 21 (72.4%) fulfilled criteria for essential tremor while 4 (13.8%) had an identifiable neurological cause. Surface EMG findings differed between functional and organic psOT, with organic cases often showing weight-bearing hyperkinesia features.

papers.title: Is Less More? Exploring the Visual Processes of Minimalist and Complex Photography Through Eye Tracking and EEG.
papers.summary: Thirty participants viewed minimalist versus complex photographs while eye tracking, consumer-grade EEG, and subjective assessments were recorded. Minimalist images elicited fewer fixations and saccades but longer single fixations, more concentrated hotspots, lower perceived complexity, greater relaxation, and higher attention eSense levels, with no aesthetic difference.

papers.title: An insular-orbitofrontal pathway supporting awareness of respiratory effort.
papers.summary: Commenting on a human intracranial EEG study using inspiratory loading, this article describes parallel insular-orbitofrontal pathways: the anterior insula signals a neuromechanical mismatch to orbitofrontal cortex for conscious appraisal, while high-frequency insular-frontal coupling supports ventilatory compensation. The authors highlight relevance for disorders of altered respiratory perception.

papers.title: EEG signature in psychiatrist's subjective experience: a pilot study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study with two psychiatrists and ten patients, the authors recorded clinician EEG during a clinical interview and ACSE administration and found dimension-specific, topographically distinct oscillatory patterns and connectivity differences for the Difficulty in Attunement and Engagement dimensions. These preliminary findings suggest clinicians' subjective experiences during clinical encounters may be associated with measurable neural signatures.

papers.title: The effect of text-picture consistency on memory integration in college students: Evidence from ERPs.
papers.journal: The British journal of educational psychology
papers.summary: In 28 college students, an adapted pictorial demonstration paradigm with simultaneous ERP recording showed that text-picture consistency improved memory integration (58% vs. 48%) and that inconsistency elicited a larger late P600 (500-800 ms) but no significant N400 difference, implicating late conflict/integration processing.

papers.title: Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation.
papers.summary: In a prospective study of 28 patients across two epilepsy centers, neuropsychological testing before and about 3 weeks after SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation found no group-level global or domain-specific cognitive decline, with only 1/28 declining on at least two measures and most patients returning to work by about 4 weeks.

papers.title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
papers.summary: This review searched three databases and identified 62 experimental animal studies (1948-2026) of corpus callosum or forebrain commissure sectioning with epilepsy-related outcomes, finding that almost none varied the extent of section or compared the three clinical extents against seizure control and cognitive outcomes. The authors argue the translational gap is methodological, requiring new animal experiments that model graded disconnection and the selective posterior operation.

papers.title: Acupotomy Alleviates Pain and Attenuates Spinal Neuronal Hyperexcitability in Knee Osteoarthritis Rats: Implication of the CaMKII/GluA1 Axis.
papers.summary: In MIA-induced knee osteoarthritis rats, three weeks of acupotomy alleviated mechanical and thermal hyperalgesia and reduced joint degeneration, with spinal RNA-seq implicating calcium signaling and synaptic transmission pathways. Acupotomy downregulated CaMKII/GluA1 expression and phosphorylation and reduced hyperexcitability of spinal substantia gelatinosa neurons.

papers.title: Vibrational dynamics of TODD-graphene nanosheets via molecular dynamics simulations and machine-learning surrogate models: implications for adaptive nanomechanical devices.
papers.summary: Using molecular dynamics with AIREBO potentials and machine-learning surrogate models, the authors characterized vibrational dynamics of TODD-graphene nanosheets, finding fundamental frequencies of 2.93–13.28 THz with f ∝ L⁻² scaling, up to 22% frequency reduction from 1 to 1000 K, and over 50% enhancement under 10% tensile strain with gauge factors of 5.3–5.7. Gradient-boosting surrogates predicted resonance frequency and quality factor with R² of 0.98 and 0.972, respectively.

papers.title: Pulsed Field Ablation for Cardiac Arrhythmias: Industry Landscape and US Food and Drug Administration-approved Platforms (2025).
papers.journal: The Journal of innovations in cardiac rhythm management
papers.summary: This review surveys the contemporary pulsed field ablation landscape for atrial fibrillation, focusing on FDA-approved platforms (PulseSelect, FARAPULSE, VARIPULSE) and next-generation dual-energy and focal systems. It compares catheter design, energy delivery, workflow, mapping integration, and clinical outcomes, framing a second PFA phase centered on procedural flexibility and lesion durability.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
